facts.function: Distributes blood to head, neck and upper limbs via brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries
facts.attachments: Continues ascending aorta at sternal angle (T4) → arches posteriorly over left main bronchus → descending aorta at T4

facts.function: Supplies posterior intercostal, bronchial, esophageal, pericardial and superior phrenic arteries
facts.attachments: Continues arch at T4 in posterior mediastinum → aortic hiatus of diaphragm (T12) → abdominal aorta

facts.function: Supplies RA, RV, SA node (~60%), AV node (~80%) and inferior LV wall via PDA in right-dominant hearts; inferior MI
facts.attachments: Right aortic sinus → right coronary sulcus → right marginal and (usually) posterior interventricular branches

facts.function: Supplies most of LV, LA and anterior two-thirds of interventricular septum
facts.attachments: Left aortic sinus → passes between pulmonary trunk and left auricle → bifurcates into LAD and circumflex

facts.function: Supplies anterior LV wall, anterior two-thirds of IV septum and apex; most commonly occluded coronary artery (anterior MI)
facts.attachments: Branch of LCA → anterior interventricular sulcus toward apex; gives diagonal and septal perforator branches

facts.function: Supplies posterior one-third of IV septum, inferior LV wall and posteromedial papillary muscle
facts.attachments: Usually from RCA (right-dominant ~70–85%) → posterior interventricular sulcus; from circumflex in left-dominant hearts

facts.function: Supplies lateral wall of right ventricle
facts.attachments: Branch of RCA → runs along acute (right inferior) margin of heart toward apex

facts.function: Supplies LA and lateral/posterior LV wall; gives obtuse marginal branches
facts.attachments: Branch of LCA → left in coronary sulcus around to posterior heart; gives PDA in left-dominant hearts

facts.function: Supplies right side of head and neck and right upper limb
facts.attachments: First branch of aortic arch → ascends behind right sternoclavicular joint → right common carotid and right subclavian

facts.function: Supplies right side of head and neck
facts.attachments: Branch of brachiocephalic trunk → ascends in carotid sheath → bifurcates at C4 into internal and external carotids

facts.function: Supplies right upper limb; gives vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical and costocervical branches; right RLN hooks beneath it
facts.attachments: Branch of brachiocephalic trunk → between anterior and middle scalenes → axillary artery at lateral border of rib 1

facts.function: Supplies left side of head and neck
facts.attachments: Second branch of aortic arch → ascends in left carotid sheath → bifurcates at C4 into internal and external carotids

facts.function: Supplies left upper limb; gives vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical and costocervical branches; proximal stenosis causes subclavian steal
facts.attachments: Third branch of aortic arch → between anterior and middle scalenes → axillary artery at lateral border of rib 1

facts.function: Drains head, neck, upper limbs and thorax into right atrium; receives azygos vein
facts.attachments: Union of brachiocephalic veins behind right 1st costal cartilage → enters RA at 3rd costal cartilage

facts.function: Returns blood from below the diaphragm to the right atrium
facts.attachments: Union of common iliac veins at L5 → ascends right of aorta → caval opening (T8) → right atrium

facts.function: Drain head, neck and upper limbs; thoracic duct enters at left venous angle
facts.attachments: Internal jugular + subclavian veins behind sternoclavicular joints → unite to form SVC; left is longer, crosses arch branches

facts.function: Carries deoxygenated blood from RV to the lungs
facts.attachments: Arises from RV conus arteriosus at pulmonary valve → bifurcates under aortic arch into right and left pulmonary arteries

facts.function: Carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs
facts.attachments: Branches of pulmonary trunk; right passes behind ascending aorta and SVC; left joined to arch by ligamentum arteriosum

facts.function: Return oxygenated blood from lungs to left atrium; ostia are common atrial fibrillation trigger sites (ablation target)
facts.attachments: Usually four (superior and inferior from each lung) → enter posterior wall of left atrium

facts.function: Drains anterior heart (LAD territory)
facts.attachments: Anterior interventricular sulcus with LAD → coronary sulcus with circumflex → becomes coronary sinus

facts.function: Drains posterior/inferior ventricles and posterior septum
facts.attachments: Posterior interventricular sulcus with PDA → coronary sinus near its right end

facts.function: Drains right margin of heart (posterolateral RA and RV)
facts.attachments: Accompanies right marginal artery → right coronary sulcus with RCA → coronary sinus

facts.function: Collects most cardiac venous blood and returns it to the right atrium; dilates with pulmonary hypertension
facts.attachments: Posterior coronary sulcus → opens into RA between IVC opening and tricuspid orifice

facts.function: Drains posterior thoracic wall (right posterior intercostals); collateral pathway between IVC and SVC
facts.attachments: Ascending lumbar/subcostal veins → ascends right of vertebral bodies → arches over right lung root at T4 → SVC

facts.function: Drains lower left posterior intercostal and subcostal veins
facts.attachments: Ascends left of vertebral bodies → crosses midline behind aorta at ~T9 → azygos vein

facts.function: Drains upper-middle left posterior intercostal veins (~4th–8th)
facts.attachments: Descends left of vertebral bodies → crosses midline at ~T8 → azygos vein

facts.function: Receives SVC, IVC and coronary sinus blood; contains SA node, AV node and fossa ovalis; forms right heart border
facts.supply: RCA (SA nodal branch usually from RCA)

facts.function: Pumps deoxygenated blood into pulmonary trunk; forms most of anterior (sternocostal) surface, most anterior chamber
facts.supply: RCA (right marginal branch) and anterior branches of LAD

facts.function: Receives oxygenated blood from four pulmonary veins; most posterior chamber; enlargement compresses esophagus (dysphagia) and left RLN
Pumps oxygenated blood into aorta at systemic pressure; thickest wall; forms apex and left border
facts.supply: LAD and circumflex; inferior wall from PDA

facts.function: Right AV valve (anterior, posterior, septal leaflets); prevents RV → RA backflow in systole; heard at left lower sternal border
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterior, posterior and septal papillary muscles

facts.function: Left AV valve (anterior and posterior leaflets); prevents LV → LA backflow in systole; heard at apex
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles; anterior leaflet continuous with aortic valve

facts.function: AV valve leaflets: tricuspid has three, mitral has two; close at S1 and anchored by chordae tendineae
Right AV valve (anterior, posterior, septal leaflets); prevents RV → RA backflow in systole; heard at left lower sternal border
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterior, posterior and septal papillary muscles

facts.function: Left AV valve (anterior and posterior leaflets); prevents LV → LA backflow in systole; heard at apex
facts.attachments: Leaflets anchored by chordae tendineae to anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles; anterior leaflet continuous with aortic valve

facts.function: Semilunar valve preventing pulmonary trunk → RV backflow in diastole; closure = P2; heard at left 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps (right anterior, left anterior, posterior) at outflow of RV conus arteriosus

facts.function: Semilunar valve preventing aorta → LV backflow in diastole; closure = A2; heard at right 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps; coronary arteries arise from aortic sinuses just above the right and left cusps

facts.function: Muscular ear-like appendages of the atria, lined by pectinate muscles; left atrial appendage is main thrombus site in atrial fibrillation
Separates ventricles; thick muscular part plus thin membranous part (most common VSD site); carries bundle of His branches
facts.supply: Anterior two-thirds: LAD septal perforators; posterior one-third: PDA

facts.function: Remnant of fetal foramen ovale in interatrial septum; patent foramen ovale permits paradoxical emboli
facts.attachments: Floor from septum primum; rim (limbus fossae ovalis) from septum secundum

facts.function: Tendinous cords that prevent AV valve leaflets from everting (prolapsing) into atria during systole
facts.attachments: Papillary muscle tips → free edges and ventricular surfaces of tricuspid and mitral leaflets

facts.function: Irregular muscular ridges lining ventricular walls; coarse in RV, finer in LV; smooth outflow tracts lack them
Ridge separating smooth sinus venarum from rough pectinate RA; SA node lies at its upper end near SVC
facts.attachments: Runs from SVC opening to IVC opening; external correlate is sulcus terminalis

facts.function: Contract in systole to tense chordae tendineae, preventing AV leaflet prolapse; RV has three, LV has two
Largest RV papillary muscle; chordae to anterior and posterior tricuspid leaflets; moderator band attaches at its base
RV papillary muscle with chordae to posterior and septal tricuspid leaflets
Small RV papillary muscle arising from septum; chordae to anterior and septal tricuspid leaflets
LV papillary muscle with chordae to both mitral leaflets; rarely ruptures
LV papillary muscle with chordae to both mitral leaflets; most prone to rupture after inferior MI (acute mitral regurgitation)
Parallel muscular ridges in auricles and anterior RA wall anterior to crista terminalis; derived from primitive atrium
Parasympathetic to heart (slows rate), lungs and gut to left colic flexure; visceral sensory
facts.innervation: CN X from medulla via jugular foramen; preganglionic parasympathetic, visceral sensory, branchial motor (pharynx, larynx)
facts.attachments: Descends posterior to lung roots → cardiac, pulmonary, esophageal plexuses → vagal trunks through esophageal hiatus (T10)

facts.function: Motor to all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid; sensory below vocal folds; injury causes hoarseness
facts.innervation: Branch of right vagus nerve (CN X)
facts.attachments: Leaves right vagus → hooks under right subclavian artery → ascends in tracheoesophageal groove to larynx

facts.function: Motor to all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid; sensory below vocal folds; compressed by aortic aneurysm or enlarged LA
facts.innervation: Branch of left vagus nerve (CN X)
facts.attachments: Leaves left vagus → hooks under aortic arch beside ligamentum arteriosum → ascends in tracheoesophageal groove

facts.function: Sole motor supply to diaphragm; sensory to central diaphragm, pericardium, mediastinal pleura (referred shoulder pain)
facts.innervation: C3–C5 ventral rami; somatic motor and sensory
facts.attachments: Descends on anterior scalene → anterior to lung root on pericardium → diaphragm

facts.function: Paravertebral ganglion chain; sends sympathetic cardiopulmonary nerves (increase heart rate, contractility) and thoracic splanchnic nerves
facts.innervation: Preganglionics from T1–L2 lateral horn via white rami; postganglionics to all spinal nerves via gray rami
facts.attachments: Lies on heads of ribs behind parietal pleura; continuous from neck to coccyx

facts.function: Carries preganglionic sympathetic fibers to celiac ganglion (foregut) and visceral pain afferents
facts.innervation: T5–T9 sympathetic ganglia; preganglionic fibers pass through without synapsing
facts.attachments: Descends on vertebral bodies → pierces crus of diaphragm → celiac ganglion

facts.function: Conducts air to lungs; C-shaped cartilage rings open posteriorly, closed by trachealis muscle
facts.attachments: Cricoid cartilage (C6) → bifurcates at carina (sternal angle, T4–T5) into main bronchi; esophagus lies posterior

facts.function: Gas exchange; right lung has 3 lobes (horizontal and oblique fissures), left has 2 lobes plus lingula and cardiac notch
facts.supply: Pulmonary arteries (gas exchange); bronchial arteries from thoracic aorta nourish lung tissue

facts.function: Transports food from pharynx to stomach; lies posterior to trachea and left atrium
facts.innervation: Vagal esophageal plexus (upper third skeletal muscle via recurrent laryngeal)
facts.attachments: Cricoid (C6) → posterior mediastinum → esophageal hiatus (T10) → cardia of stomach
facts.supply: Thoracic: esophageal branches of aorta; abdominal: left gastric artery

facts.function: Primary muscle of inspiration; contraction flattens domes, enlarging thoracic cavity
facts.innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5): 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive'
facts.attachments: Xiphoid, lower 6 costal cartilages, L1–L3 (crura) → central tendon; IVC T8, esophagus T10, aorta T12
facts.supply: Pericardiacophrenic, musculophrenic, superior and inferior phrenic arteries

facts.function: Fibroserous sac enclosing heart; fluid in pericardial cavity (between parietal and visceral serous layers) causes tamponade
facts.innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5); pericarditis pain referred to shoulder
facts.attachments: Fibrous pericardium fused to central tendon of diaphragm and adventitia of great vessels

facts.function: Remnant of fetal ductus arteriosus (shunted pulmonary trunk blood to aorta); left RLN hooks around arch beside it
facts.attachments: Connects origin of left pulmonary artery to inferior surface of aortic arch

facts.function: Formed by LV; site of apical impulse (PMI) and mitral valve auscultation
facts.attachments: Points anteroinferiorly to the left, at left 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line

facts.function: Posterior surface formed mainly by LA (with some RA); receives the pulmonary veins
facts.attachments: Faces posteriorly toward T6–T9 vertebrae; separated from esophagus by pericardium (oblique sinus)

facts.function: Cardiac muscle layer of heart wall; generates pumping force; thickest in LV
facts.supply: Coronary arteries; drained by cardiac veins to coronary sinus

facts.function: Carries right bundle branch from septum to anterior papillary muscle, coordinating its contraction; prevents RV overdistension
facts.attachments: Interventricular septum → base of anterior papillary muscle of RV

facts.function: Semilunar valve cusps; close in diastole to prevent backflow, producing S2 (A2 then P2)
Semilunar valve preventing pulmonary trunk → RV backflow in diastole; closure = P2; heard at left 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps (right anterior, left anterior, posterior) at outflow of RV conus arteriosus

facts.function: Semilunar valve preventing aorta → LV backflow in diastole; closure = A2; heard at right 2nd intercostal space
facts.attachments: Three cusps; coronary arteries arise from aortic sinuses just above the right and left cusps
